title: Protocol to assess human glioma propagating cell migration on linear micropatterns mimicking brain invasion tracks
protocol: Cover PDMS stamps with a solution of laminin.
Remove excess laminin solution from the stamps.
Carefully press the stamps onto the surface of the imaging dish to imprint the desired features.
Passivate the rest of the surface to prevent cell attachment outside of the stamped areas.
For routine migration assays, create micropatterns on 35-mm plastic bacterial plates.
For TIRF or confocal imaging, make micropatterns on glass-bottom dishes that have been silanized first.
Perform passivation with pluronic solution for plastic surfaces.
Use PLL-g-PEG working solution for passivation on glass surfaces.
Coat coverslips with PLL-g-PEG for deep UV photolithography.
Burn the coated coverslips with desired features using a photomask and deep UV.
Acid wash and air-dry coverslips.
Place coverslips in a holder for plasma cleaning.
Plasma clean coverslips.
Coat PEGylated coverslips with PLL-g-PEG.
Position PEGylated coverslips onto the chrome mask using milliQ water.
Place the chrome mask into the deep-UV machine with coverslips facing down.
Lift coverslips from the chrome mask using milliQ water.
Mount micropatterned coverslips in magnetic imaging chambers.
Transfer dishes under a biosafety cabinet at end of steps 2 and 3 for sterile handling.
Incubate glass-bottom dishes in silane solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Remove silane solution from glass-bottom dishes.
Rinse three times with methanol on a rocker for 5 minutes each time.
Remove the methanol and air-dry the dishes under the chemical hood.
Proceed with the stamping procedure as indicated in step 2.
Cut out the desired features from the stamps using a scalpel.
Place the cut-out stamps in a small culture dish, features facing up.
Expose the stamps by removing the lid of the dish.
Place the dish in the plasma cleaner and start the vacuum pump.
Switch ON the plasma cleaner for 3 minutes.
Add 20 μL of laminin solution (50 μg/mL in DPBS) on top of the stamps.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 30 minutes.
Hold the stamp using tweezers.
Air-blow dry all laminin on the stamp.
Turn the stamp upside down and press it gently onto the imaging dish.
Lean the side of the stamp onto a kimwipe.
Air-blow dry the stamp after leaning.
Remove the stamp from the imaging dish in one motion without shaking.
Add 2 ml of pluronic solution per plastic dish for incubation.
Add 300 μl of PLL-g-PEG working solution per glass-bottom dish for incubation.
Incubate at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 1 hour.
Aspirate the solutions from the dishes under a biosafety cabinet.
Replace aspirated solutions with 2 ml sterile DPBS in each dish.
Rinse the dishes 5 times with dPBS.
Replace rinse solution with 2 ml GSC medium and 40 μl of growth factor mix per dish.
The dishes are now ready for cell seeding.
Pick up the coverslips from the ethanol solution and dry them one by one with an air-gun.
Transfer dried coverslips to a clean rack.
Place the rack containing dried coverslips in a plasma cleaner.
Start vacuum pump and switch ON plasma cleaner for 3 min.
Drop 100 μL PLL-g-PEG working solution on the bottom of a petri dish covered with parafilm.
Flip coverslips onto PLL-g-PEG drops.
Incubate coverslips at room temperature (20°C–25°C) for 1 hour.
Rinse coverslips in milliQ water using a beaker.
Dry coverslips on paper towel, PEG-PLL facing up.
Clean photomask with isopropanol and carefully dry it with kimwipe or airflow.
Place photomask under deep UV for 5 min (golden side facing up).
Drop 4 μL of milliQ water onto the desired pattern of the photomask.
Flip coverslip on drop, ensuring PLL-g-PEG is in contact with mask.
Remove bubbles between mask and coverslip by gently pressing with tweezer.
Wear protective nitrile gloves when manipulating the mask to avoid leaving fingerprints.
Remove bubbles from the mask to ensure they do not interfere with the design.
Place the mask, golden side facing down, under deep UV light for 10 minutes.
Detach coverslips by spraying milliQ water onto them; do not force detachment to avoid smearing PLL-g-PEG.
Rinse detached coverslips in milliQ water and transfer them to an imaging chamber.
Coat the coverslip with 10 μg/mL laminin diluted in sterile DPBS and incubate at 37°C for at least one hour.
Rinse the coverslip two times with DPBS.
Replace rinse solution with 2 mL GSC medium and 40 μL of growth factor mix.
The dishes are now ready for cell seeding.
Evaluate the density of hGPC tumor-spheres under a microscope (10× objective) after 5 days in culture.
Transfer the content of the dish into a 15-mL tube for hGPCs.
Centrifuge the sphere suspension at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate the supernatant from the centrifuged sample.
Add 1 mL of GSC medium to the pellet after aspirating the supernatant.
Triturate by pipetting the suspension up and down 100 times with a P1000 pipetman set at 800 μL for hGPCs.
If necessary, further triturate by pipetting 20–30 times to ensure no spheres remain.
Transfer between 1/20 to 1/3 of the cell suspension volume to a new 6-cm culture dish containing 4 mL of GSC medium and 80 μL of grow factor mix.
Seed cells on laminin-coated plates for transfection and/or migration assay.
Passage the cells again after 5 days.
Detach hGPCs from their plate and count them.
Electroporate one to two million hGPCs with 10 μg of DNA using the Neon™ Transfection System 100 μL Kit.
Replate electroporated hGPCs on a laminin-coated dish.
Aspirate the medium from cells for transfection.
Rinse cells with DPBS.
Add 0.5 ml of trypsin/EDTA to a 6-cm dish and incubate for 2 min at 37°C.
Inactivate trypsin with 3.5 ml of GSC-BSA medium.
Transfer the cell suspension in a 15-mL tube.
Transfer 10 μL of cell suspension and count the cells in a cell counting chamber.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 × g.
Aspirate the supernatant, add 4 mL of DPBS to the cell pellet, and centrifuge for another 5 min at 200 × g.
Aspirate the supernatant and re-suspend the cell pellet with buffer R in order to obtain 1–2 × 10^6 cells / 100 μL.
Place the cuvette in the Neon electroporator and add 3.5 mL of buffer E2.
Ensure that the cuvette clicks inside the slot in the Neon electroporator.
Avoid wetting the electrical pads located between the cuvette and the Neon electroporator.
Add 12 μL of DNA to a 1.5 mL sterile Eppendorf tube.
Add 120 μL of cell suspension in buffer R to the tube.
Mix gently up and down the cells with the DNA.
Set the following parameters on the Neon electroporator: Voltage: 1,600 V, pulse duration: 20 ms, number of cycles: 1.
Pick up the tip for electroporation with the Neon pipette.
Take 100 μL of cell suspension-DNA mixture and insert it into the cuvette along with the tip.
Hit “Run” on the Neon electroporator.
Transfer the electroporated cells directly to a 35-mm bacterial plate that was previously coated with laminin.
Change the medium after 6/8 hours from transfection if cells are well adherent on the dish.
Check the cells and change the medium the day after transfection.
Trypsinize and transfer cells to another dish if needed.
Culture hGPCs on a laminin dish for imaging and transfection.
Aspirate the medium from cells previously seeded on laminin.
Rinse once with DPBS.
Incubate cells with 500 μl of trypsin/EDTA for 1–5 min at 37°C.
Resuspend the cells with 3.5 ml of GSC-BSA medium to neutralize the trypsin.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 5 min at room temperature (20°C–25°C).
Aspirate the supernatant.
Re-suspend the cells in 4 ml of GSC medium.
Count 10 μl of cells using a cell counting chamber.
Seed 2,000–100,000 cells on patterned dishes depending on the pattern and size of the cells.
Incubate at 37°C for 3–4 h.
Gently rinse with warmed medium to get rid of floating cells before imaging.
Place imaging dishes in the plate holder.
Allow cells to stabilize for at least 30 minutes before recording.
Select positions to record using the software interface.
Adjust focus using the camera.
Set the exposure time, light power, time length of acquisition, and acquisition rate.
Start imaging.
If cells were transfected with a fluorescent construct, acquire the corresponding fluorescent channel to track the transfected cells.
Open one imaging file with Fiji (Schindelin et al., 2012).
Go to Plugins, then select tracking and manual tracking.
Paste tracks in Excel and make calculations to extract speed and persistence.
Hit the button “Add track” in the tracking window.
Click on the cell to track: after each mouse click, visualize the following image of the temporal stack until the last image is reached or the “End track” button is pressed.
Save and open track files in excel for analysis.
Open a Microsoft Excel workbook.
Activate the Developer tab.
For Windows, click “File”, then “Options”, then “Customize Ribbon” and flag “Developer”, then click “Ok”.
For macOS, click on “Excel” in the menu bar, then “Preferences”, then “Ribbon & Toolbar”, flag “Developer”, and save.
Select “Macro Security” in the Developer tab.
In the window that opens, flag “Enable all Macros” and “Trust access to the VBA project object model”, then click “Ok” for Windows or “Save” for macOS.
Click on “Visual Basic” in the Developer tab.
The Visual Basic Editor appears.
On the top left, click on “Insert Module”.
Select all the text from https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fnprot.2014.131/MediaObjects/41596_2014_BFnprot2014131_MOESM399_ESM.txt.
Copy and paste the selected text into a blank window.
Repeat steps for https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fnprot.2014.131/MediaObjects/41596_2014_BFnprot2014131_MOESM400_ESM.txt.
Repeat steps for https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fnprot.2014.131/MediaObjects/41596_2014_BFnprot2014131_MOESM394_ESM.txt.
Download other programs for further analysis from https://www.nature.com/articles/nprot.2014.131.
Save the workbook as Excel Macro-Enabled Workbook (.xlsm).
Make a copy of the .xlsm file just saved.
Copy the slice number of the trajectory from the trajectory file.
Paste the slice number in column D (or 4) of a worksheet.
Copy the X coordinates from the trajectory file.
Paste the X coordinates in column E (or 5) of the worksheet.
Copy the Y coordinates from the trajectory file.
Paste the Y coordinates in column F (or 6) of the worksheet.
Ensure numbers start from 1, have no space between rows, and increase monotonically.
Rename the current worksheet (e.g., “Condition 1”).
Repeat steps for new worksheets if additional conditions are present.
From the Developer tab, click on “Macros.”
Select one of the installed programs and hit “Run.”
Plot the data using GraphPad Prism 9.0.
Copy the data into a column tab in GraphPad Prism 9.0.
Focus on the last point for cell persistence analysis.
Go to the worksheet “LastPoint” in the Excel workbook.
Copy the data highlighted in Figure 5F from the "LastPoint" worksheet.
